title: A prompt is a contract
summary: Structure a prompt around a goal, context, constraints, and verifiable success.

scenario.briefing: The team wants an AI colleague to draft a function. A vague request produces confident guesses. Arrange the parts of a prompt that can be evaluated.

objectives.description: Order the parts of an evaluable prompt.
Explain what makes a prompt testable.

hints: Start with the task and the context the model actually needs.
Constraints and non-goals prevent unwanted changes.
Success criteria and output format make the result checkable.
Order: goal, trusted context, constraints, success criteria, output format.

misconceptions.description: Putting format before the goal and constraints.
misconceptions.feedback: A format without context or constraints gives the model no basis for the content. State the goal, context, constraints, and success criteria before the format.

misconceptions.description: Trusting the model to certify its own output.
misconceptions.feedback: A self-check can help, but the contract needs externally observable criteria that a test or reviewer can apply.

sections.title: State the job precisely
sections.body: A useful prompt names the goal, supplies only relevant context, states constraints and non-goals, and defines what success looks like. Output format belongs in the contract when another tool or person must consume the result.

sections.title: Prompts do not replace verification
sections.body: A clear prompt improves the chance of useful output but cannot guarantee correctness. The engineer still reviews the result, runs tests, and checks assumptions against evidence.

vocabulary.definition: A prompt with explicit goal, context, constraints, and success criteria.
A change intentionally excluded from the task.
The required shape of the response.

steps.title: Arrange the prompt
steps.prompt: Order the sections of a prompt for drafting a stock-check function.

items.label: Context: function is used by the checkout service
Constraints: no new dependencies, reject non-integer quantities, preserve existing callers
Success: boundary tests for 0, negative, exact stock, and over-stock pass
Output: one JavaScript function plus its test cases

steps.explanation: Goal and context establish the task. Constraints narrow acceptable solutions. Success criteria and output format make the result checkable.
hints: Start with what the model must achieve.
Add the material it needs before the rules that constrain it.
State the constraints and the evidence of success before the output shape.
Order: goal, context, constraints, success criteria, output format.

steps.title: What makes a prompt useful?

statements.label: Success criteria make output easier to evaluate.
Requesting tests from the model removes the need to run them.
Relevant context helps more than unrelated background.

steps.explanation: A prompt contract improves direction, but execution and independent review remain the engineer's responsibility.
hints: A contract names observable success, not a feeling.
Constraints tell the model what it must not do.
A self-check is useful but does not replace measurable criteria.
Select criteria, constraints, and context; reject the claim that asking the model to check itself is enough.

accessibility.summary: Prompt sections can be reordered with buttons and are read as an ordered list.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use move up and move down buttons. Drag and drop is optional.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each section announces its position and full text after every move.
